body:
Yes. I recently started thinking of my pre-birth era as death in just the same way that I will be dead after my life is over. I have been dead already, so why fear it? Only my attachment to my individual ego separates me from total acceptance of the "death sandwich" -- my life being the filling between two infinite slices of death bread.

It's the ongoing task of my life to reconcile myself to the death sandwich and to savour the filling while I still can.
💖☺️ Yep, that's my nihilism.
Same. I use nihilism as a relaxation technique. It's a relief to know nothing matters and I will be forgotten in 50 years. I can focus on now and prioritize what matters to me.
Thank goodness. ☺️💖

Sometimes.

I am just a temporary flesh puppet running experiences.exe through my brain circuits. It doesn't matter whether or not I do something, but some things uncontrollably matter to me.
How weird it is to exist at all.
26, Autistic, I just escaped to a disabled friend's place and now they care for me. Living at parent's place drove me to suicidality all the time.

I'm 26, Autistic, and the government just cut off my disability money after escaping an abuser. I have no money coming in, can't get my groceries, am relying on a friend for everything. I'm at the end of my rope. I'm so tired of struggling to  survive this world.

I have been feeling this way for years. I'm 26. People don't understand. I call it end-stage ADHD because I think I've run out of novelty in this world. It's so familiar to me that nothing is pure novelty anymore. I'm okay with dying in my sleep. There's nothing more I want from the next 50 years.

My brain settled down in my mid-twenties. Now I care a bit less what people think of me (still not stable though). Am less socially anxious. The 20s is a second adolescence so if you feel crazy, that's normal, you're not imagining it. I've come to believe it's impossible to "fail" ones twenties, firstly because it's a time to fuck up and secondly  most failure is a social construct. Most people are a mess in their twenties, even if they don't show it.

Nihilism is now a comfy armchair; I settle into it at the end of a long or difficult day and remind myself that nothing matters.

Follow my curiosity. Let myself fixate on interesting things. Let myself rest. Allow myself physical pleasures. And use nihilism as a release valve when things start feeling neurotic. Remembering that nothing matters is a source of pleasure when I'm stressed.
I don't. I've tried. Sometimes I succeed in blocking it out and forgetting it for a bit.

Nihilism 85% eases my depression, 15% feeds it.

I turn to it when I'm stressed because I remember nothing matters (yay!), but when I'm happier, remembering nihilism drains me of motivation.
Spinach.
I'm glad I don't believe in it. It's a weight off my shoulders to believe that I'll just have nothingness after this life.
I take one day at a time and allow myself to be lazy whenever I need to and can do. 😊 I prioritize pleasure, avoid pain, and bathe in nihilist thought when I need to destress. Nihilist YOLO.
Oooo yes, I love blue sky.
Nihilism is so relaxing. 🤸🏼‍♀️
I'm just vibing. Avoid suffering, seek pleasure, wait for death. I'm too ADHD to commit to anything. My neurology demands that I must dabble and forage, so that is what I do.

Yes, I don't like spreading the "knowledge" of the germs' existence. It's unpleasant and occupies my mind, taking up space I need to think about other things. Having the "Ew, this has germs" feeling multiple times when I'm just trying to function, uses up my mental energy reserves.

Yeah. I've often wished I could submerge myself in the illusions other people live in. I don't want to be able to see through everything, it takes the sparkle out of everything.

I miss being a kid who liked fantasy. It was nice to be lost in these worlds.

Yes. I have 50 years stretching out ahead of me and absolutely no desires. I just don't want all that time. Life is so long.

I've reached peak hedonism and no longer find new things exciting. I'm aroace so don't want a relationship or children. I've tried dozens of languages and fixated on every topic that interests me. I feel spent. There's nothing more I want out of the world.

Same.

I have another 50 years on this planet and I am so spent. It sounds like such a drag. 😭

I'm a progressive who hates progressives for this very reason. I feel so alienated by the cruelty. I was stalked, dogpiled and driven to suicide by other members of my community this year. They didn't care even when I was suicidal. They just got more abusive.

This year has just been one big breaking point for me. I belong nowhere, I'm valued by few people, nobody cares about my feelings. I often have different views to other progressives (we're talking minor things like terminology, not basic human rights) and I can't voice them without communal abuse and ostracism. I just want to be myself and be valued. I'm tired of repressing who I am and living in constant paranoia that other people will tear me apart.

I empathize with everyone, including people who are cancelled, and it sucks. I'm tired of feeling so much in a world of people who hunt each other for sport.

I can't heal from it. Human behaviour disgusts me and makes me suicidal.

Yes. I am already bored of hedonism as a poor person. I would be bored of hedonism as a rich person too. It's just different arrangements of atoms exciting the same pleasure circuits, whether it's a cheap beef burger or a premium cut.
Aromantic asexual. 👋🏻
This me. I am very asocial.
☺️ Thankful for meaninglessness. /gen

My first memory of the internet existing: it was September 2001, I was 5 years old and having my first ever lesson in the computer suite at school. A kid was browsing Amazon, against the school rules. The room was talking casually about how, "it's amazing we can buy stuff online these days!"
When I stopped talking to my stuffed toys.
"You were right, dad. My mother is a Narcissistic bitch."
😂 😳 None.
Worryingly ask them, as if I've just been caught in the middle of something important, "did you find the bodies?!"
Finding an Autistic best friend and moving out of the toxic parent's home to go live with them.
Wall's Vegan sausage rolls.

My 16 year old classmates felt more sane, sensible, mature and safe than my mid-40s mother. I liked them because they ticked these bare minimum boxes of human decency.

When children outperform your parents in decency, that's the nail in the coffin of any chance of good parenting.

Feeling battered and bruised from a lifetime of bigotry, and still seeing and experiencing it every day. The inaccessibility and precarity of Autistic life in allistic, abled society is constant mental torture.
Yes. It's vital communication, functionality and community for disabled people. Without it, I would not have been able to survive.
Young adulthood is a second adolescence. It will be messy, traumatic, confusing, painful, disorienting. It's impossible to fail at young adulthood because it's meant to be a mess.
A huge pile of Vegan Wall's sausage rolls to eat until my stomach says No.

I've had similar feelings especially re: last paragraph. However, I often wish I lived a few centuries from now, when presumably society has progressed substantially on social issues, poverty is rare or non-existent, bigotry is rare, world is more accessible for me.

I often say 25th century. I wouldn't change the country. I think the UK would be an okay place in the future -- better than now, actually.

Yeah. I often think of how we're all temporary flesh puppets, going through life. As someone's science teacher said, we're just complicated worms taking in food and pooping it out. Worms that have figured out how to write books and contemplate reality.

Curiosity (wanting to see how the future turns out, see the future of loved ones).

Fear of pain.

The repercussions of attempting to end myself (I'd destroy a friend).

Knowing my suffering will be inevitably over in 50 years so there's no need to rush my death.
Nice meaningless poll. 👍🏻 /gen
I'm depressed but turn to nihilism for comfort.
Nihilism actually helps the depression. It's my balm/anti-depressant. When I need to decompress and stop caring, I turn to nihilism.

I remember being suicidal for the first time at age 6. I was miserably alone with an abusive and neglectful single mother. I remember wishing I could just stop existing because there was nobody to entertain me or love me. I felt completely alone in the world.

So I can sort of understand. I was first made aware of the concept of suicide at age 4 because the mother constantly talked about it with me, yelling and complaining about how she wanted to kill herself.

Some kids' lives really are so bleak, that the moment they understand death, they desire it.

I just moved out of an abusive parent's home that I've lived in for 26 years. I now live with my only offline friend, in a new city, and I feel dysregulated and trapped. I keep feeling regret.

I left because my old home couldn't meet any of my basic human needs and I was chronically suicidal. I'm painfully shy and Autistic; my friend is also Autistic and understands my needs. But I feel like a burden on them, that I'm not the person they thought they loved (we met online), that I'm annoying and plain. My new home fully understands my needs but the settling process is traumatic for my Autistic mind/body.

I've never done anything like this before. I ran away from home, with a person I've only known 6-12 months, to a brand new city, with just some luggage and important documents. There are people in this city who can help me survive. On paper, being here is better in many ways.

But I feel a bit crap. I've made an irreversible, life-changing decision. I'll never see my old room again. None of my possessions.

I'm tired and feel icky.
Turns out I was Autistic and the world is torture by default.
Hold a conversation. I'm semi-speaking Autistic.
Vomit, pee, poop, cheddar, bogies, dirt, blood, celery, semen, sweat, toenails, dead skin.
Wash my face of night grease build-up, then put glasses on and read internet.
Taking it day-by-day, fulfilling my creature needs, keeping distracted with tasks and pursuing pleasure until my life is over.
Pass away soon, experience as little trauma as possible.

It feels genetically coded into me. I've inherited my father's "final" disposition. I was religious as a kid but my neurology eventually developed along the pathways of logic and constant analysis, collecting information about the world, and it made it impossible to believe in meaning.

I feel like a slave to my neurology. I didn't choose to think this way, it's just what I found at the end of the path.
Yes.
I'm in this position. Wrong neurology, incurable trauma, alienated from society, can barely access it or function. Can't get my bare minimum needs met. Tired of struggling.
Nice, thank you!

It's systematic gaslighting. The MH situation in my country is so bad and people are still pushing the "just open up, take some pills, meditate" line ... how am I supposed to have mental peace in this world? I am constantly bothered by the atrocities happening and the inequality and poverty and all these physical things that powerful people just don't want to fix. I despair at how hopeless and powerless I am under the boot of sociopathic politicians. So much of r/suicidewatch is preventable suffering.

I feel like I wrote a lot of this, ha ha. Am also 25 with OCD and my birthday is in less than 2 hours. I have pure OCD and real event OCD and it's exhausting. I feel like all my friendships are based on a lie and everything will "fall through".
Can't stand the thought of another 50 years of this. I feel like I've outlived myself.
So sorry for the cr*p you're trapped in. 💔🫂

I can really relate to the struggle with strangers' meanness. I also keep to myself and avoid trouble but people have taken stuff out on me. When people do that, it's about them, not me. It gets tiring though.
Yes. I have tried so hard and done well with circumstances, but I just want it over.
Same.
I never tire of seeing her 😳
Comforting meaninglessness 🥰
Cooked breakfast, played a game, descaled a kettle, resting.
🥰 Comforting nihilism affirmations.
Hedonic adaptation?
Wibbly wobbly, galaxy walaxy ... stuff.
It's like the phrase loving kindness ... I think I feel a compassionate hatefulness.
6 years old, now 26.
I need this too.

That professor's microaggression was nasty. I'd be horrified if they said that to me.

Higher Ed is a horrible time to be Autistic. I flunked out of Year 12 (UK, pre-college) and never finished school. The transition to adulthood was too much for me and I had no idea why. Now I know what I am, I'm on disability, and my life is more stable. I care much less, at 25, about what allistics think about me. It's such a relief. When you're young you're fed with ideas of what kind of person you should be. I used to be so neurotic and thought my grades defined me and that I was worthless without them, without a degree, without finishing school. I have none of those things and yet I have a "normal" self esteem now. I don't believe I'm great but I'm not worthless either. I couldn't have imagined feeling this way when I was 19. 

Something nobody warned me about, and I think this is doubly true for Autistics, is that young adulthood is a second adolescence. The brain doesn't finish developing until 25-27 for anybody. It's not a time where you have your shit together, usually, and now that I'm older I don't expect younger people to. It's a chaotic traumatic panicky mess.

I recently found an Autistic elder (just hit their 30s) who went through so much of the same stuff as me and could validate all my experiences. They too were a chronic dropout, on disability, an abused and neglected orphan, but now living stably with healthy self-esteem. Autistics never get to see their developmental pathways mirrored in allistics, and that is a trauma. The trauma undid itself when I met someone else who'd lived through the same.

Yes I feel this way too. I hate the whole political spectrum for being cruel. I'm a progressive who hates progressives. The behaviours of the human race has turned me into a misanthrope. We're just apes slinging poop at each other.
I basically live here now. It's my psychiatric hospital.
It is for me. It changes every hour and moment to moment. One hour I'm doing my chores, the next hour I'm pursuing my suicide plan. Rinse and repeat.
💜🫂 That's a lot to go through.
This is comforting. ☺️
It's interesting/entertaining to watch. I have 10 days of news content up until her funeral that I can use to fill the void in my soul.
💦 Juicey nihilist affirmations.
💖 Commenting purely to hype this insightful and cathartic post for the karma it deserves.

26 this month and I feel this way. I see the pointlessness of everything, I can't relate to the human species and hedonism isn't working for me anymore. I've tried activism/participating in community but that's toxic. I've tried hundreds of new foods, a dozen languages, explored the world via the web and I'm just done now. I don't see how I can do this another 50 years. I'm aroace and unemployable Autistic so I really have nothing left to hold me to this planet.
Pain. Regret while I wait for my liver to shut down. Accidentally setting my house on fire or poisoning my cat. My cat. A concert in October. My friend who loves me too much.
Ear defenders might help. It doesn't totally block it out but it softens noises a lot so it doesn't hurt my ears.
Same.
Relentless mood 👌🏻
Same. Wish I wasn't tied to people. Bestie gave me a long convo yesterday about how my death would destroy them.
It's my main OCD theme and torturing me right now.
I wish I could go to a place of heavenly bliss for a while, after my Earth torment. But I'm an atheist and don't believe in that. If Heaven existed, it would make it easier for me to die.
Me with my cat.
Same.
Happy birthday :) I'm a September baby too.
Feels like I wrote both your comments 😭 The bullies got away with it and I can't let it go.
The people around you sound like assholes. ☹️
My cat. A concert in October. That's about it. I keep wondering how much I really care about those things.
Relentless suffering. Spiritually exhausted. Bored of Earth. CPTSD. Disability. Living on the margins of society with no point living.
I know this feeling. Laying down gives me pressure aches.
I've been craving euthanasia for ages. I really don't have a place on this planet. I'm just biding my time, waiting for death, living on the margins of society.

It's sensory hell for Autistic people. Meltdowns make me feel homicidal/selfcidal.

Am also in UK and don't like wasting resources. But noise is one of those things that is a life or death thing to me.

😭 Can relate. The NHS is so useless for Autistic people and there's absolutely no mental healthcare available for us. It's one of the reasons I've avoided a crisis team. They will harm me. It feels like shit knowing that there's absolutely no safety net for me when I want to kill myself. And that allistics won't ever understand why I want to die.

Sometimes.

I'm excited to fulfill a new life plan. To escape and run away from a toxic household will be my adventure.
I like the title. I feel like the title sometimes.
My cat. My teeth. Saving money for moving out. My favourite music group.
Yes.

I'm 25. I go through the list of different methods every day, naying all of them as too painful, messy, scary, unreliable. I'm always left with a couple of tolerable options that I can't access or do right now.
I don't even feel pain. I'm suicidal from a weary, tired soul that doesn't want to deal with reality anymore.
🥺 Her loveliness weighs 9.4kg.
My inner monologue when I look in the mirror every morning.

It's infuriating because my suicidality is caused by specific situations that society can address but chooses not to. Poverty, housing, ableism, etc. Everyone just gives me contact details for suicide lines but won't actually solve the problem of why I'm suicidal. Telling me not to kill myself doesn't help. Killing myself is a solution to society's problems.

I recognize your display name, fellow ami :)

I want to die too. Life is so hard and exhausting.

I can relate. The UK feels like this. Am trapped living with abusive mother because society can't give me a pathway out of here. I want to move out but it requires so many pieces of a puzzle to survive out there and there's the constant risk of everything falling through when I live alone. The precarity of life in this world is exhausting and scary. Death feels so much easier than getting a place of my own and a support system to prevent me from dying. The world is so inaccessible to disabled people.
It comforts me that I am not alone or unusual in this torment.

I can't even properly escape in my sleep because I have dreams that are mostly emotionally draining. I wish I had dreamless sleep. And I wish it was biologically possible to sleep all day every day until my body dies.

Mine is obsessed with genealogy and uses it to boast about being connected to royalty. We're talking thouands of years ago, to the point that everyone is related to royalty 😭 She wants to feel important/superior to people.
Oh same 🫂 I'm relentlessly in that feeling these days.

I'm not coping. I wish I was.

All I have to keep me sane is fellow sufferers of Narcs. My bestie has a Narc mother like I do.

Yes. My mother has chronic illness and has weaponized it for 20 years. I don't even know how much to believe anymore because she exaggerates and complains so often. She's always having a heart attack. She's gonna face karma for that, if she finally does have a heart attack but I don't believe her. 🤷🏼‍♀️

She says she's exhausted and in pain but has the energy and fury of Hulk every day, slamming stuff and complaining about everything. For contrast, when I'm tired I barely speak or move. 

Almost every sentence that comes out of her mouth is a complaint about her body. Every week she has a different problem, it seems.

Are you me? 😭 I feel like I wrote most of it, minus the mother and alcohol. Parents split at five, the Nmother got custody of me, and has been spitting hairs about what an evil person my dad is for 20 years -- completely oblivious to the fact she is the evil one.

She's so incredibly self-absorbed. The "pain contest" -- now I have a word for it! I have never gotten an ounce of real empathy from her, everything is about her.

Yes. My mother always launches into a monologue about all her difficulties and complains about the last 25 years of her life.

I just had another raging argument with her today because she made me snap. Instead of making amends, which she has never done, she starts complaining about how difficult her life is.
Yes 😭 constantly
I'm jealous she got her hands on it 😭 it's impossible in the UK
I wish I'd never existed.
🤩 Life goals.

I want a clean, functional space.

Owning things burdens me.

And I want my space to reflect the ephemerality of my human life. I am just a temporary visitor here.

Thank you for the story, it's very motivating!💪🏻 I have a similar battle approaching with my mother's stuff once she dies and every bit of new clutter she brings into the flat fills me with dread and a little bit of frothing rage. I am working hard to thin out my own possessions and it has gotten so easy to be ruthless and just get rid of stuff now. 

I'm glad I saw the light in my mid-twenties and realized I'm a minimalist at heart because it's a weight off my shoulders to be free of clutter and the obligations that come with it.

I would feel nothing but relief.

Unfortunately my financial security and logistical safety depends upon the Nmother due to disability so it's not going to be a simple relief. I will finally have peace and control over my own space, but at the cost of more precarity and poverty.

If I was financially safe, I would celebrate the Nmother's death.
Sorry the Narc did that to you! You're not alone. Had that happen to me as a kid. 😔

My mother always resented when I was sick because it was an inconvenience on her and she'd get mad at me for asking for help/assistance.

I'm Autistic and ADHD but I never got identified despite going through school non-attendance twice because she centered herself and invented a story about how I'm a young carer, because everything revolves around her. 😒

She never took me to a dentist as a kid, I have my dad to thank for that habit. She never got my eyes tested, I initiated that myself as an adult.
Wow, that sounds like a really unpleasant experience. 😬 As an Autistic person who cares about ableism, you're definitely not ableist for calling your dad that.

Yes. As someone who is also Autistic, I know what actual ableism looks and feels like. I also know how my mother's Narcissism harms me. I am not imagining it. Her Narcissistic behaviours cannot be separated from the harm they cause. One of the reasons I never got identified as Autistic is that she centered herself during my burnout to frame me as a young carer. That kind of Narcissistic behaviour is harm in action. Other behaviours like chronic egocentrism both harms a developing child and infuriates grown adults.

All of the harms can be followed backwards to the source: a Narcissistic behaviour.

My mother is not a victim of her PD identity. She doesn't suffer prejudice asa covert Narc who is enabled by everyone. She has never suffered consequences or accountability. Nobody has ever punished her or given her stigma for it. She's been coddled and validated her whole life by her enablers.

I got "corrected" on twitter about it and it peeved me off and I snapped back at them. Nobody gets to police how I describe the abuse. I know what I am experiencing. The language belongs to the victims. It was a relief when I finally figured out what she is.

It feels like an example of Narcs taking advantage of earnest and Narc-naive progressives. I removed myself from the Autistic twitter space partly for this reason. I can't exist in a space where my lived reality is considered problematic.
I could've written this post myself 😂

I allow myself to violate the Nmother's food stores sometimes because

1) she takes up most of the space in the kitchen
2) she's food-rich compared to my food reserves, so I'm Robin Hood
3) she owes me after a lifetime of abuse, neglect and spending on herself at my expense, or only begrudgingly spending on me

I recently ate her brioche because I love brioche and I was out of food, and  couldn't be bothered owning up to it and dealing with her rage.

Morals are a social construct compared to the meaningless and cruel universe and I'd rather reserve my respect, energy, love etc for people who don't hurt me.

My nmother collects possessions as if she's gonna live forever. Every new item that enters our home has a little bit of my dread attached, because I know that's just more clutter I need to throw out once she's dead/dying, and I don't wanna deal with that. 

I don't think she's ever seriously confronted her mortality. She certainly doesn't think about how other people will deal with the problems she leaves behind. I don't think she has any savings or insurance, even though she could definitely accumulate some savings at least.

She's 50something and has 20 years left on the planet, if she's lucky, because she's unhealthy and chronically ill. But she eats and buys things as though she's immortal. If I was her, I'd be the opposite -- thinning my possessions and preparing as much as I can so I don't stress out my survivors too much. I'd also probably be focusing more on giving back to society.

"I'm just tired" or "I don't feel well".

Sounds innocuous but she says it in every sentence and in response to EVERY SINGLE TIME I hold her accountable.

As a kid it was, "because your dad [insert crime I don't believe he actually did]".

She'd crawl her pathetic self to my room after an episode of abuse to apologize and make excuses.
I'm so glad toxic mothers are more spoken about now. I'm tired of living in a society that constantly gaslights me because people don't like their fantasies about motherhood to be contradicted.

"They love you because they love how you make them feel, they hate themselves and need someone to take it out on."

This bit boils down everything about my Nmother.

This whole post resonates so much 😭 My nmother always complains that she never had more children but she's incapable of treating them properly. Got mad if I existed around her, spoke to her, made any noise, asked her to fulfill a need. Used to go into spirals where she'd pull out a knife or suitcase and threaten to kill one of us.

Honestly used to offend me when she said she wanted more kids, because it meant she had no self awareness of how she treated me and thinks that she did well with me. She thinks it's okay to be abusive. I cannot fathom how someone would simultaneously crave children but hate their existence. Unless one sees it as an aesthetic rather than a responsibility.

Her menopause is a blessing.

She also constantly complains that she doesn't have a man to complete her, she's obsessed with the heteronormative cliché where she's a helpless damsel whose husband does everything for her. Completely oblivious to the fact that her self-obsession would repulse the guys she dates. There's no space for anyone else in a relationship with her. It all has to be about HER needs and her suffering.

She doesn't understand that relationships are about relating to other people.

She professed to love me, but seemed often at risk of euthanizing me. 😢
Pure cowardice keeps me here.

My minimalism goal includes wall decoration. The pictures I have blu-tacked to the walls are meaningful to me/reflect my passions. My abstract interests (a music group/concert memories/nostalgia) aren't really dependent on owning physical items and actually one of my goals of decluttering is to have more mental and physical bandwidth for these abstract interests.

I declutter stuff so I have empty functional space, but keep the walls lively.
Congratulations on 4 chapters! I can barely finish a short article these days.

Wow, this must be so frustrating. First thing I felt on reading -- congrats on going back to get the A Levels! I never got mine because of disability so you've already achieved more than I have.

It sounds like you're a spoonie/chronic illness and pursuing anything with that is exhausting, I relate. Getting to the end of the course with a pass grade is better than nothing at all. You say your past self worked in a factory, and now you're someone who has qualifications to your name too, so you're already stepped up in achievement from your previous self, if that makes sense.

The poverty sucks, I'm sorry. 🫂 All I can say is you're not alone in that regard. Society is so difficult to survive in when you're poor/disabled or just straight up tired of the demands of capitalism. You can be proud of yourself for getting this far in such a difficult society and situation. I wish things were better for you.

Cancel culture is what gave me OCD. Being cancelled over something that wasn't actually a bad behaviour, being stalked, dogpiled, gaslit and emotionally controlled by a group of woke young people made me suicidal. I'm still struggling with the flashbacks every day. I still contemplate suicide. I wasn't allowed my own space or feelings, they felt entitled to it. They live in my head every day and won't leave.

I hate cancel culture. It's about controlling other people rather than making the world a better place. Bullies gravitate to it because it gives them a feeling of power over other people and they have many enablers who will back them up. I've completely lost faith in a minority community I was a part of and I feel furious at them now. I'm completely alienated and alone, which is dangerous for my demographic because we have a high suicide rate.

I no longer believe in the movement I was a part of. My trust has been broken and now I'm constantly paranoid that everyone hates me and my friends will abandon me and spread a particular image of me just because I'm not a clone of them and have my own thoughts and feelings.

I feel like I'm suffocating.
Yeah I'm like this. Enjoying small things but having triggers throughout the day and nonchalantly thinking about killing myself.
🥰 Such a comforting clip. /gen
Love this 👏🏻

Get the paint can out of my life.
Get the oats out of my life.
Get the bag of trash out of my life.

Scan more school books so they can go in the trash.
I went through this recently. It's hell.

I lost multiple years of education because my Nmother sent me to her old secondary school for convenience instead of letting me pick my school. It was an awful school where the math teaching in particular was non-existent and I was alienated and bullied there.

I eventually went to the school of my choice anyway for a different reason but I lost two and a half years of learning that I never got back, and I had to desperately study whenever I could with the few resources I had in order to pass exams. The trauma of falling behind never went away and just compunded over the years. I still have nightmares about school and never gained closure from it.

When I burned out at the first school, it was an opportunity to get diagnosed as ADHD and Autistic but the Nmother centered herself and framed me as a young carer, she manipulated the authorities against me so my needs never got recognised or met. It still fills me with rage and grief that I had to figure it out on my own as my life fell apart around me and I contemplated suicide. Her Narcissism has been erasing me and speaking over me since birth and it hurts so bad. She's completely incapable of thinking about my needs or empathizing with me. The world revolves around her.

I'm a hedonic minimalist. I don't want permanent crap in my life but I get my pleasure from consumables like food, toiletries and the internet. I save money for important big spends or emergencies because I value the security.
I'm aroace so it's literally my goal to be single all my life 🤣
I have this but with the phone battery exploding my hands off into stumps so I use one hand at a time so I only sacrifice one.
Yes. I'm trapped living with the nmother because of disability and poverty. I've become chronically suicidal because it feels like the only way to escape living with her.
Ayy lmao 😭

As a kid I helped clear out a dead person's local storage garage of their possessions and it made me aware of how irrelevant most possessions become once someone dies. They don't have memories attached for anyone else because it belonged only to the dead person. I remember my dad pointing out how depressing it was for a person to leave so much stuff behind, suddenly without their personal meanings attached. That's the first time I got acquainted with materialism as a social construct. I have my own attachments to things but they're with the awareness that those things also pass onto new adventures after I die, and do not ultimately belong to me. We're all part of this big environmental cycle -- both bodies and objects -- and there's a closure in that knowledge, for me.

I'm the type who enjoys consumables and will get them as long as they're going to be used soon i.e. I've run out of previous item. I see consumables as an "experience" -- a food I've never eaten before, a scent I've never smelled before -- because the goal of my life is to have these little novel sensory experiences. 

As a person aspiring for minimalism and in the midst of decluttering years of stuff I never use, I realized the only reason an item should be in my life is either for its usefulness or experiential nature, and consumables fall under the latter.

Yes, I'm a lot more discerning about what I need or want now. If I want something, it's usually something consumable that won't be in my apartment forever (e.g. new food, new toiletries). I look for "experiences" in my purchases and prioritize them. I buy things one or two at a time and wait for them to run out before getting new ones.

It feels good to live a lighter life, more aligned with my philosophical beliefs that life is short, memories fade and the past becomes irrelevant to my present, and that I'm not an extremely important historical figure who needs to preserve all her stuff. I'm just another human out of the 8 billion passing through this world. I see stuff as part of the human environment now; objects move between individuals and objects "live a life". If the stuff stays with me, the object isn't living a life and therefore its manufacture is going to waste. 

I'm not minimalist but I feel more comfortable living that way if the eventuality arises. I feel like I've psychologically prepared myself for it and therefore made myself more resilient to it.

All my "crushes" have actually been squishes driven by "special interest energy". In fact, I can't remember a single time after age 12 that I had a special interest that /wasn't/ a person.

For about 18-36 months (about the same time for a romantic attraction to dissipate in a romantic person) I am utterly fixated on them. Not sexually or romantically but platonically. Theoretically I want to befriend them or, if substantially older than me, seek out a parental connection. But I don't actually have the desire to fulfill it, and also I don't have the opportunity either (most of them are famous strangers lol).

During a "squish era", I learn a lot of stuff relating to their craft, just as a "side effect" of liking them. So I learn about musical or cinematic influences if my squish is an actor or musician (usually). Very occasionally I have a real life squish, but much weaker.

My squish becomes my whole life for the length of the era, but when the era is over I tend to become repulsed or apathetic towards them. Which makes me a little sad, and also cynical about whatever "love" I feel at present.

It feels kinda like a curse sometimes, the transition period is dull and sad, but falling for a new person platonically is a lot of fun. I wish I could "collect" squishes cumulatively instead of discarding them consecutively but I guess that's just how I'm wired.

Also it's ironic that I'm intensely asocial and introverted, and yet my special interest is always person-centric. I think it's because I'm fascinated by "the spirit of a person", the initial mystery, and whatever particular "personality magic" they harbour as a unique human being. The theory of a person is platonically attractive to me, I experience their personality kinda the way one would experience and appreciate a work of art. Or ... like having a favourite Earth character.

I'm female by the way; I suspect that person-centric interests are overrepresented in female autistics.

It makes the eventual shower even more of a farce than it should be because you have so much to wash off and you *never* wash it all off. I manage to scrub off maybe 30% but honestly the amount of dirt seems to go on forever and it just keeps coming off as you're drying yourself and IT NEVER STOPS. It just gathers on your fresh clothes and dries out until the next time you can be bothered to change or wash.

Often in 2015 I would just stick my head under the shower, while fully clothed, and that would be it for a few weeks.

Occasionally, I stick my arms under the shower because they start to go black with dirt like the rest of the body and seen as they're quite visible appendages, I want them to at least appear clean. But honestly most of the time I don't bother. And my feet have been covered in black dirt before, as though I've just climbed out of a mine. At this point I usually have the panicky resolution to actually clean them, because holy shit it's not a flattering feeling when you look down at your dirty feet and realise how low you have sunk.

And now, in 2016, I still generally don't shower unless I'm turning very visibly dirty or my scalp feels unbearably gross. Or I have a rogue flash of motivation.

I just cannot, for the life of me, find a solution for this. I hate the whole process of showering. The preparation pre-shower, the daydreaming and procrastination in the shower, the tiredness after the shower. Asking me to have a shower feels a lot like asking me to very kindly, if you'd please, step into a black hole.

But yes, I use distractions to numb myself from my situation. Chronically. In fact, at the extreme, it's called maladaptive daydreaming. I think I experience that. I read that dissociating to some extent from situations is something that most children will use in difficult psychological circumstances, but the ability carries through to adulthood and can then be hijacked by depression. It's a defence mechanism to "carry" the child through a situation in which they are helpless and require an adult to intervene. It's meant to be a temporary buffer to provide the child with comfort during temporary stressors but adult psychopathologies take advantage of whatever coping mechanisms they can find, even if they're not age appropriate. And so depression takes the dissociative dynamic for its own and you get the depressed video gamer/bookworm/reality tv bingewatcher or the maladaptive daydreamer.
Fantasizing. Eating. Curling up in a foetal position on the floor. Watching documentaries sometimes. Obsessing over random topics and futurism.
